articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Sevilla vs Osasuna
articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del Sevilla vs Osasuna, que se juega este lunes 26 de octubre en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, correspondiente a la décima jornada de LaLiga 26/27
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del Sevilla vs Osasuna, que se juega este lunes 26 de octubre en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, correspondiente a la décima jornada de LaLiga 26/27
articles.body: El conjunto hispalense llega en la parte alta de la tabla, sexto tras nueve jornadas con 14 puntos. El Osasuna, con 11, vive un momento de transición, con el regreso de Jagoba Arrasate al banquillo, y busca romper su mala dinámica lejos de casa. Favorito para el partido entre Sevilla y Osasuna Con estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito al Sevilla, aunque sin una diferencia demasiado amplia. Codere paga su victoria a cuota 1.90, una cifra moderada que refleja que los locales parten por delante, pero sin demasiado margen. El Osasuna llega con la moral reforzada tras vencer 2-0 al Racing de Santander en el estreno de Arrasate. Ante un rival que ha marcado diez goles en nueve partidos, su triunfo en Sevilla se paga a 4.00. Ante Budimir, con siete goles en Liga, el Sevilla tendrá que cuidar mucho su área. El empate, a cuota 3.40, cobra relevancia en un cruce igualado, en el que los precedentes recientes reparten los puntos con frecuencia. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes de las apuestas deportivas. El Sevilla ha encajado 16 goles en nueve jornadas y llega con varias bajas en su plantilla, entre ellas Marcão, Guridi y Sierra, además de la duda de Kochorashvili. Con estos datos, Codere paga el Sí a 1.92, una cuota atractiva para un equipo local que no termina de cerrar su defensa. Por otro lado, el Osasuna ha encajado 18 tantos, pero ha firmado solo diez a favor, lo que demuestra que no siempre encuentra la portería. Si el Sevilla se adelanta y gestiona bien el partido, el No gana peso y se paga a 1.8. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con presencia de tantos. En lo que va de Liga, los partidos del Sevilla acumulan más de tres goles de media, y los del Osasuna rondan esa cifra. Ninguno de los dos aparece como un bloque sólido en defensa. Por eso, la línea de 2.5 goles resulta asequible para el Over, que cotiza a 2.10 en Codere. No obstante, la llegada de Arrasate puede traducirse en un Osasuna más ordenado y compacto, algo que le llevaría a jugar con el partido controlado y pocas ocasiones. En ese escenario, un 1-0 o un 1-1 dejaría el marcador por debajo. El Under 2.5 se paga a 1.65. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Sevilla juega en casa con la intención de buscar amplitud por las bandas, con jugadores como Félix Correia y Rubén Vargas, lo que suele generar saques de esquina si el rival se encierra. El Osasuna, por su parte, podría adoptar una actitud compacta durante largos tramos, lo que favorecería un buen volumen de córners para los locales.

articles.title: Rusia volverá a ser sede del Mundial de un deporte olímpico más de ocho años después
articles.standfirst: Desde febrero de 2022, cuando comenzó la guerra en Ucrania, Rusia ha estado proscrita por las federaciones internacionales
articles.summary: Desde febrero de 2022, cuando comenzó la guerra en Ucrania, Rusia ha estado proscrita por las federaciones internacionales
articles.body: El Kremlin celebró este lunes la decisión de la Federación Internacional de Halterofilia (IWF) de celebrar el Campeonato Mundial de 2030 en Moscú. "Rusia debe retornar de pleno derecho a la familia deportiva mundial, porque esta familia no puede vivir plenamente sin la participación rusa", aseveró durante su rueda de prensa telefónica diaria el portavoz de la Presidencia rusa, Dmitri Peskov. La IWF anunció este domingo que la capital rusa será sede del Mundial de 2030, decisión que marca un nuevo paso hacia el retorno de Rusia al calendario de las grandes competencias internacionales. Será el primer Mundial de un deporte del programa olímpico que se celebrará en Rusia desde febrero de 2022, cuando comenzó la guerra en Ucrania. La decisión fue adoptada por el Comité Ejecutivo de la IWF, que confirmó que Ahmedabad, en India, recibirá el Mundial de 2029, y asignó los Mundiales juveniles de 2028 a Pristina, en Kosovo, y los juveniles Sub 20 a Caracas, Venezuela A la vez, en respuesta a la posibilidad de que Rusia acoja unos Juegos Olímpicos en un futuro, Peskov llamó a "no adelantarse a los acontecimientos". "Ahora en realidad no son muchos los países que se muestran interesados en convertirse en sedes de Juegos Olímpicos. Es necesario equilibrarlo todo, las cosas a favor y en contra de las decisiones correspondientes. De momento, el asunto no está en el orden del día", indicó. Rusia fue siempre sede habitual de grandes campeonatos y en los últimos años, antes de atacar Ucrania, había organizado hasta una Copa del Mundo de fútbol en 2018.

articles.title: NHL Trade Rumors: Dylan Larkin deal could be closer than expected as Red Wings face critical days
articles.summary: NHL trade rumors around Dylan Larkin have reached a potentially important stretch, with a prediction pointing to late October as a possible window for a
articles.body: NHL trade rumors around Dylan Larkin have reached a potentially important stretch, with a prediction pointing to late October as a possible window for a deal. Detroit has reportedly explored young centers around the league, while Larkin has widened the list of teams he would consider joining. Those developments have added urgency to a story that has lingered for months, but they are not proof that a trade is close. The Red Wings still need an offer that meets their expectations, and Larkin must approve any destination because of his full no-trade clause.NHL trade rumors put Dylan Larkin in focusOn October 16, analyst John Buccigross said on Frankly Hockey that he expected a Detroit trade within seven to 10 days. When Frank Seravalli asked if he meant Larkin rather than defenseman Simon Edvinsson, Buccigross confirmed Larkin was the player he had in mind. That forecast placed the possible window around October 23-26.On October 22, NHL insider Elliotte Friedman reported that the Red Wings had asked other teams about young centers, including prospects who have yet to play in the NHL. Friedman could not confirm whether those conversations involved Larkin, Edvinsson or both. The discussions point to broader roster planning, not a confirmed trade plan.Larkin has also reportedly expanded his list of acceptable destinations from three teams to 10. The clubs named in reports include Colorado, Minnesota, New Jersey, Dallas, Washington, Carolina, Tampa Bay, Florida, Vegas and Utah. A longer list could give Detroit more room to negotiate, though Larkin would still have to approve the team involved.Detroit’s asking price could decide the outcomeThe bigger obstacle may be what the Red Wings want in return. TSN’s Darren Dreger has reported that Detroit is seeking two high-end prospects, a top-nine NHL forward and a first-round pick. That is a steep package, even for a proven center who could strengthen a contender.Some possible destinations may struggle to meet that price. Colorado has been linked as a fit but faces questions over available assets and salary-cap space. New Jersey’s situation may have shifted after its reported Connor Hellebuyck trade, while Minnesota could have a limited offer to put together. These are potential complications, not signs that talks with any one club are close.Detroit has good reason not to move Larkin for a disappointing return. He is a top-line center, and accepting less than the club believes he is worth would weaken its position. But a high asking price can also narrow the market if interested teams cannot assemble the right mix of players and picks.The late-October prediction may prove accurate, but it is still a forecast. If those days pass without a deal, that would not automatically mean negotiations have collapsed. The key question is whether Detroit can find a return it likes and a destination Larkin will accept. Until both conditions are met, trade talk remains just that.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: What happened when NHL linesman Travis Gawryletz accidentally struck Pittsburgh Penguins captain Sidney Crosby during the game against Nashville Predators
articles.summary: During a game against the Nashville Predators, NHL linesman Travis Gawryletz accidentally struck Pittsburgh Penguins captain Sidney Crosby, leading to a dramatic 3-2 overtime win. Despite the collision, Crosby continued to play and assisted in the tying goal before securing victory for his team.
articles.body: Pittsburgh Penguins captain Sidney Crosby was accidentally struck in the face by NHL linesman Travis Gawryletz during the first period of Pittsburgh’s game against the Nashville Predators on October 24. The unexpected contact knocked Crosby to the ice, but he was able to continue playing.The unusual incident became one of the game’s most talked-about moments. Crosby later assisted on Pittsburgh’s tying goal, and the Penguins completed a comeback with a 3-2 overtime victory at PPG Paints Arena.What happened when Travis Gawryletz made contact with Sidney Crosby?The collision occurred in the opening minutes of the first period as Crosby moved across the ice. Gawryletz was extending his arm to signal an onside play when his arm caught the Penguins captain in the face. The unexpected contact sent Crosby down to the ice.The incident appeared accidental rather than a deliberate action by the official. Crosby had been skating toward the play when the linesman moved his arm outward, leaving the captain caught by surprise.The brief collision stood out because it involved a player and an on-ice official rather than contact between opposing players, and it also happened early in a game that would eventually develop into a closely contested matchup between Pittsburgh and Nashville.Was Sidney Crosby injured after the accidental hit?Crosby did not appear to suffer a serious injury from the collision and continued participating in the game. Reports said he briefly stepped away from a faceoff to check on his face and speak with the linesman before returning to the action.There was no indication in the available reports that the incident forced Crosby to leave the game. His subsequent contribution to Pittsburgh’s comeback also showed that he remained involved in the contest.The moment drew attention because of the unexpected nature of the contact, but the game continued without a reported extended stoppage related to the collision. The incident was not described as a deliberate hit or a disciplinary play.How did Sidney Crosby help Pittsburgh Penguins beat Nashville?Despite the unusual opening-period moment, Crosby played a role in Pittsburgh’s late comeback. With the Penguins trailing 2-1 in the third period, he delivered the pass that allowed Rickard Rakell to score the tying goal with 1:06 remaining in regulation. The assist was Crosby’s 1,111th with Pittsburgh, tying Hall of Fame defenseman Ray Bourque for the most assists with a single NHL franchise.Pittsburgh then completed the comeback in overtime. Ville Koivunen scored at 3:44 of the extra period to secure the 3-2 victory, giving the Penguins two points after they had trailed late in the game. Connor Dewar also scored for Pittsburgh, while Steven Stamkos and Jayden Struble found the net for Nashville.The result gave the Penguins consecutive wins after a four-game losing streak, adding significance to a night that featured both an unusual on-ice collision and a dramatic finish.Crosby’s response ensured the accidental contact did not define his performance. Rather, his assist on Rakell's tying goal and Pittsburgh's overtime victory became significant parts of the story of the game, and the collision with Gawryletz was a memorable and surprising moment of the NHL contest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Connor McDavid puts the NHL on notice as his latest Oilers run sparks a major conversation
articles.summary: Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid has reached a remarkable milestone by recording 31 points in his first 10 games of the 2026-27 NHL season, joining the ranks of Wayne Gretzky, Mike Bossy, and Mario Lemieux. In this article, we explore his record-breaking performance and what it means for the Oilers' season.
articles.body: Connor McDavid has joined Wayne Gretzky, Mike Bossy, and Mario Lemieux in an exclusive NHL scoring club after recording 31 points in his first 10 games of the 2026–27 season, and the Edmonton Oilers captain reached the milestone with a five-point performance in a 6–5 shootout victory over the Carolina Hurricanes on October 22.McDavid’s tally includes eight goals and 23 assists, making his start one of the most productive opening stretches in NHL history. The 29-year-old also surpassed Gretzky’s previous Edmonton franchise benchmark for points through the first 10 games of a season.Connor McDavid joins NHL legends after historic Edmonton Oilers startConnor McDavid became the fourth player in NHL history to record at least 30 points in the first 10 games of a season. He reached the milestone during Edmonton’s 6–5 shootout win over the Carolina Hurricanes, finishing the night with two goals and three assists.McDavid’s fifth point against Carolina came as he helped set up Leon Draisaitl’s power-play goal. He later scored again to tie the game at 5–5 with less than two minutes remaining in regulation, before Edmonton secured the victory in a shootout.The performance marked his third five-point game of the season. McDavid had previously recorded five points against the Vancouver Canucks on October 1 and the Utah Mammoth on October 17. His consistent production has helped him open the campaign with a point in each of Edmonton’s first 10 games.Which NHL legends achieved the milestone before McDavid?McDavid joins three legendary players who have hit 30 points in their first 10 games of a season in three different eras of NHL scoring.Wayne Gretzky: 30 points in 10 games for Edmonton Oilers in 1984-85.Mike Bossy: Also hit 30 points in the first 10 games of the 1984-85 season with the New York Islanders.Mario Lemieux: Did it three times with the Pittsburgh Penguins, in 1988-89, 1992-93 and 1995-96.Lemieux remains the standout in this category, having recorded 37 points through the first 10 games of the 1988–89 season, and McDavid’s 31-point total places him among the most prolific opening stretches in league history, although it does not surpass Lemieux’s mark.What does Connor McDavid’s historic NHL start mean for Edmonton?McDavid’s early production has given the Edmonton Oilers a major offensive boost. He is averaging 3.1 points per game, and that rate would translate to 260 points across an 84-game regular season if maintained. That figure is a projection, not a prediction, and sustaining such production over a full campaign would be an extraordinary challenge.Draisaitl, McDavid’s longtime teammate, praised the captain’s form after the Carolina game. According to NHL.com, Draisaitl described McDavid’s production as “just not real” and said it was a pleasure to share the ice with him. The comment reflected the remarkable level of performance McDavid has delivered early in the season.McDavid has also set a new Edmonton franchise benchmark for points through the first 10 games, moving beyond Gretzky’s previous mark of 30 in 1984–85. The milestone adds another chapter to his career with the Oilers, where he has played throughout his NHL career since being selected first overall in the 2015 draft.The immediate challenge is sustaining his production as opponents adjust their defensive plans, and McDavid’s speed, playmaking, and ability to create scoring opportunities have made him difficult to contain, but the remaining schedule will test whether he can continue at anything close to his current rate.For the Oilers, his form offers an encouraging start to the season, particularly when combined with Draisaitl’s contributions, and Edmonton’s 6–5 shootout win over Carolina showed how McDavid’s production can influence close games, with his late tying goal helping the team extend the contest.McDavid’s 31 points are already a historic achievement, regardless of what follows. The Oilers captain is off to one of the most sensational starts to the 2026–27 NHL season and is in elite company with Gretzky, Bossy and Lemieux. Whether he can challenge more scoring records is a question that remains to be answered and depends on his continued production, his health and the Oilers performance over the months ahead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mountain West Connection Football: MW Week 8 Players of the Week
articles.summary: Major upsets are shaking up the conference
articles.body:
Week 8 brought major developments in the Mountain West race, with Wyoming knocking off Air Force, New Mexico handing North Dakota State a costly defeat, Hawai'i rolling past Northern Illinois and Nevada earning a much-needed Homecoming win over San José State.

The weekend featured explosive offensive performances, defensive plays that decided games and a special-teams return that helped swing momentum. With New Mexico and Wyoming strengthening their positions near the top of the conference standings, here are this week's Mountain West Connection Players of the Week.

Offensive Player of the Week: Tyler Hughes, Wyoming

Hughes delivered one of the weekend's most complete performances, leading Wyoming to a 28-14 victory over Air Force in Laramie.

The Cowboys quarterback accounted for 259 total yards and three touchdowns, combining 146 rushing yards with 113 passing yards. He averaged more than 12 yards per carry and finished without a turnover against an Air Force team that entered the game with one of the conference's most dangerous rushing attacks.

Hughes immediately put pressure on the Falcons, opening the scoring with a 68-yard touchdown run. He also threw touchdown passes to Jake Wilson and Samuel Harris before Wyoming added a fourth-quarter rushing score to seal the victory.

The performance was especially important for a Wyoming team that has steadily improved after a difficult start to the season. The Cowboys are now 5-3 overall and 4-1 in conference play, putting themselves firmly in the Mountain West championship conversation.

Hughes earns this week's offensive honor for his ability to hurt Air Force with both his arm and his legs while protecting the football.

Defensive Player of the Week: Austin Brawley, New Mexico

New Mexico's 21-16 victory over North Dakota State featured a defensive play worthy of deciding a major conference matchup.

With the Lobos clinging to a five-point lead in the fourth quarter, defensive back Austin Brawley intercepted North Dakota State quarterback Nathan Hayes and returned the ball 56 yards for a touchdown. The score gave New Mexico the cushion it needed to survive the Bison's late push.

North Dakota State scored again but could not complete the comeback, as New Mexico forced a turnover on downs to secure the win.

Brawley's interception was the defining moment in a game where points were difficult to find. The Lobos also recorded nine tackles for loss, disrupting the Bison's running game and forcing Hayes to shoulder more of the offensive burden through the air.

New Mexico held North Dakota State to 16 points and secured one of its biggest victories of the season. The Lobos improved to 6-1 overall and 3-0 in conference play, while Brawley's pick-six proved to be the difference.

Special Teams Player of the Week: Ky Woods, Nevada

Nevada needed a spark against San José State, and Woods provided it at a crucial moment.

The Wolf Pack led 21-10 in the fourth quarter when the Spartans scored a touchdown to cut the margin to 21-13. Woods responded with a 90-yard kickoff return, setting Nevada up in excellent field position and changing the momentum immediately.

On the very next play, running back Dominic Kelley punched in a four-yard touchdown to restore Nevada's 18-point advantage. The Wolf Pack went on to win 28-13.

Woods' return was the turning point in a game where Nevada's defense had controlled much of the action. The Wolf Pack held San José State to just 70 total yards through the first three quarters and limited the Spartans to 179 yards for the game.

Nevada improved to 3-4 overall and 2-2 in Mountain West play. Woods' return did not go for a touchdown, but its timing and direct impact on the scoreboard make him a deserving special-teams selection.

Micah Alejado, Hawai'i — Offense: Alejado threw for 323 yards and three touchdowns in the Rainbow Warriors' 56-21 victory. His passing performance helped Hawai'i produce its highest-scoring outing of the season.

Luke Duncan, Nevada — Offense: Duncan completed 18 of 29 passes for 178 yards and two touchdowns without an interception in Nevada's 28-13 win over San José State. He delivered career highs in passing yards and touchdown passes.

Wyoming defense — Defense: The Cowboys forced three Air Force fumbles and recorded seven tackles for loss, disrupting a Falcons offense that had been difficult to contain throughout the season.

Dominic Kelley, Nevada — Offense: Kelley carried the ball 24 times for 82 yards and a touchdown, helping Nevada control possession and close out its Homecoming victory.

Week 8 reinforced how quickly the Mountain West race can change. New Mexico strengthened its position at the top with a win over North Dakota State, while Wyoming continued its climb with a statement victory over Air Force. Nevada also showed signs of progress by combining a disciplined defensive performance with timely special-teams execution.

Hughes was the weekend's most productive offensive player, Brawley delivered the defensive play of the week and Woods supplied the momentum-changing return. Meanwhile, Hawai'i's blowout win offered a glimpse of what its offense can accomplish when everything clicks.

With the season entering its final stretch, every conference victory carries added weight. New Mexico and Wyoming have put themselves in strong positions, but Week 8 showed that the race remains far from settled.

articles.title: Inside how the Seahawks defense dominated the Chiefs in Week 7
articles.summary: Inside the numbers of how the Seattle Seahawks defense dominated the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks played complimentary football throughout Sunday's dominant 20-3 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs . The defense especially dominated on primetime in Week 7. It was an elite effort from Mike Macdonald's unit.

The previously 5-0 Chiefs failed to score a touchdown . Per NFL research, that's the first time the Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs did not reach the end zone in 153 career starts for the MVP-winning quarterback. That includes postseason appearances.

Former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker has been excellent for the Chiefs this season. The Seahawks totally suffocated him and Andy Reid's running game. Walker, the league-leading rusher, was limited to 36 rushing yards on 14 carries; he averaged just 2.6 yards per attempt, a career-low mark.

Mahomes was 19-of-33 for 165 yards and an interception. No Chiefs pass catcher reached 50 receiving yards.

The Seahawks outgained the Chiefs 410-213, nearly doubling their offensive output. The Seahawks also dominated the time of possession battle 35:51-24:09. That's a credit to both the offense and defense.

An all-around effort from the Seahawks included an elite defensive showing. It was a big-time win for the previously .500 Seahawks, who improved to 4-3 and kickstarted their 2026 season with a statement win.

articles.title: SEC Standings: Where does Oklahoma fit in conference title race
articles.summary: A look at the SEC Standings after Week 8 action. Where do the Oklahoma Sooners fit into the SEC Title race.
articles.body:
Through Week 8 of the 2026 college football season , the race for the SEC title game is wide open. There are two teams with just one loss in conference play, and there are eight teams with two losses. Midway through the season, 10 teams are still in the mix for a spot in what is expected to be the final SEC championship game.

To everyone's surprise, the Kentucky Wildcats lead the standings at 5-1 in conference play. Georgia trails the Wildcats by a half game at 4-1 in league play.

Despite how the season has started, the Oklahoma Sooners still have an outside shot at making the title game. They have to run the table to make it to Atlanta, but it's possible if they get a little help from around the league.

articles.title: 3 stars from Week 7 for the 49ers: Slim pickings after an off game
articles.summary: We went with three players on the 49ers offense
articles.body:
It was ugly, it was sloppy, and it was bad. But somehow the San Francisco 49ers found themselves with a chance to take the lead with three minutes left in the fourth quarter.

Brock Purdy's second interception of the game killed that hope, and the 49ers suffered their first loss of 2026, falling 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons. Since the Arizona game, it's felt like the 49ers' first loss was coming, but San Francisco staved off defeat with back-to-back one-possession wins before finally succumbing to Atlanta.

With the 49ers taking a 6-1 record into the bye week, these are the three stars from the Week 7 loss:

Let's get it out of the way now: the fumble sucked, and it was the first sign that Sunday might not be the 49ers' day. But on a day where the defense had no standouts, Black's first NFL touchdown and his performance in relief of McCaffrey were good enough to earn the third star, despite the fumble.

With McCaffrey missing most of the first half, it was on Black to step up. And it was a rough start for the rookie. His day opened with a run that lost four yards, a play blown up by Kendal Daniels. He'd get back to zero yards with his next touch, but it wouldn't be until his fifth carry to get his rushing yard total greater than zero.

But then Black would explode from there. The 49ers' third drive would start with an 11-yard catch from George Kittle, but it would be all Black from there. He would move the 49ers into plus territory with a 15-yard run followed by a gain of seven. Black would close the drive with a mostly untouched 30-yard touchdown run to put the 49ers up 14-3.

His next and last impact on the game would be his fumble, but it was an encouraging overall performance with 12 carries for 63 yards and the touchdown in the spell of McCaffrey.

Sunday's loss was such a stinker that half the reason Kittle earned the No. 2 star is that it was a good game on National Tight End Day.

Kittle celebrated the occasion with a game-high eight receptions for 88 yards, responsible for 30 percent of the 49ers' passing offense.

The tight end's day started with a 17-yard reception with the 49ers facing a third-and-4 on the team's second drive of the game. He'd then open the 49ers' next drive with an 11-yard catch to start what would end up being a touchdown-scoring drive.

He'd have a few more short receptions before closing his day with his longest reception, a 21-yard catch, but Kittle fumbled for the 49ers fourth turnover, ending the 49ers slim hopes of a comeback.

Not the best game from the People's Tight End with the turnover, but a good enough performance on a holiday he created (although Kyle Juszczyk being called an "honorary tight end" should be enough to end the gimmick) to earn a star.

Just like with Mike Evans last week against Washington, McCaffrey's knock on Sunday completely hampered the 49ers offense.

It was painfully obvious Sunday was a scheduled McCaffrey game, with the 49ers running back getting six touches of the 49ers' 10-play opening drive. He would take those touches and give the 49ers 69 total yards, ending the drive with a one-yard touchdown run to put San Francisco up 7-0 early.

The 49ers' second drive would start with Purdy connecting with McCaffrey for a five-yard pass with a little under seven minutes left in the first quarter. That would end up being McCaffrey's last touch until the 8:15 mark in the third quarter, with the running back dealing with a thigh injury for most of Sunday.

In the time McCaffrey was off the field, the 49ers offense had three drives that lasted a combined 18 plays for 122 yards, ending in a punt, touchdown, and a fumble lost (on a drive. San Francisco had six drives with McCaffrey on the field, running 47 plays for 281 yards with two touchdowns, but the four others ended in some type of turnover, none at the fault of McCaffrey.

Three drives without McCaffrey averaged six plays for 41 yards, while the six with the running back averaged nearly eight plays for 47 yards. McCaffrey finished Sunday with 13 touches for 100 yards (his second 100-yard game in a row) with the touchdown. Curious just how different Sunday's game could have gone had McCaffrey not missed those two drives. Nonetheless, his performance was easily the best by a 49er in Atlanta.

Throughout the season, we will track the three stars of the season by tallying points for each star award using a complex scoring system: three points for being the first star, two for the second, and one for the third. Through Week 7, the standings are:

articles.title: The Penguins saw the old Rickard Rakell on Saturday. They need that guy back
articles.summary: Down 2-1 on Saturday night with the clock ticking away, the Penguins got a signature goal from their three best players on the ice to tie the score. Erik Kar...
articles.body:
Down 2-1 on Saturday night with the clock ticking away, the Penguins got a signature goal from their three best players on the ice to tie the score. Erik Karlsson and Sidney Crosby assisted on Rickard Rakell's late score to tie the game. It was a goal the team desperately needed, and the type of play they haven't made that often early in this year Crosby making a wonderful pass to put a winger in position to score, and then the winger actually scoring.

Unsurprisingly, it was a weight off Rakell's shoulders to tally just his second goal of the season that is now 12 games old.

"It felt so good. The amount of looks I had – first off, in this game – my teammates setting me up for all these chances, it definitely feels good to put one in," Rakell said after the game .

Despite the lack of results, Rakell has been generating chances. He's earned that good feeling and confidence boost from scoring due to all the chances that he's created. Rakell was stopped on a breakaway earlier in the game, and even before that few players in the league have generated as much as Rakell has at 5v5. This data is before the Nashville game, even then, Rakell didn't score a 5v5 goal (since the Penguins had pulled their goalie, it was a 6v5 situation).

Rakell has 30 shots on the year, enough to lead the team by a wide margin (Kris Letang, Ben Kindel and Nick Robertson all have 23 a piece). It's no secret or deep analysis that the Penguins need Rakell to pitch in. Rakell scored 59 goals in the last two full seasons from 2024-25 to 2025-26, in the ballpark with names like Kirill Marchenko, Brock Nelson, Bo Hovat and not too far off Sidney Crosby (62).

Rakell isn't a player the team can afford to have in a slump and expect to get good results. The team's record in first 11 games of the season illustrate that, as did Rakell stepping up to score Saturday in a game the Pens found a way to win in overtime.

The stakes are only raised now that Bryan Rust is on the shelf with injury for at least six weeks, the importance of a player like Rakell only gets magnified when another one of the tried-and-true options is unavailable.

The good news for the Pens may be that Rakell has been generating all those chances, it would be a more difficult conversation to have if this was a player failing to even get in position to score. That hasn't been the problem to this point. It's been about finishing those chances, which can be an area that ebbs and flows for even the most consistent and reliable players over stretches to go hot and cold. For someone as skilled as Rakell, enough chances will lead to goals eventually. Such was what happened on Saturday, getting a prime chance sent his way by Crosby, and then finally breaking through to put the puck in the back of the net.

Rakell was cold early in the season, the Penguins could sure benefit from it if the late goal in their last game was a sign that he is coming out of it and about to start filling the net, as he typically will do over the long haul. The Pittsburgh first line needs it, the power play needs it and the team at large would be in for a big boost if some more red lights behind the goalie follow from the chances Rakell has been generating in front of him.

articles.title: Conte breaks silence amidst reports he could return to Juventus
articles.summary: Several reports have linked Antonio Conte with a return to Juventus and a possible move to Manchester United, with both clubs reportedly considering changes...
articles.body:
Several reports have linked Antonio Conte with a return to Juventus and a possible move to Manchester United, with both clubs reportedly considering changes in the dugout. Conte continues to be associated with Juventus, particularly as Luciano Spalletti faces pressure following a difficult spell at the club.

The Bianconeri have been linked with bringing Conte back on several occasions , and speculation could grow if results fail to improve. The club are also working to ensure they have the right players and managerial leadership to meet their objectives.

John Elkann has shown a willingness to dismiss managers when performances fall below expectations, and there are growing concerns that Spalletti could lose his job in the coming weeks. Some Juventus supporters would welcome Conte's return, although there is no confirmation that the club are preparing to appoint him.

Conte has a strong connection with Juventus, which means his name is likely to feature whenever the club's managerial position comes under scrutiny. However, speculation about a potential reunion does not necessarily mean negotiations are taking place.

(Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Manchester United also linked with Italian coach

Manchester United are another club reportedly considering their options. Michael Carrick could face dismissal before Spalletti, while Conte has reportedly been included on the Red Devils' list of potential managerial candidates.

Some reports have even suggested that Manchester United have held advanced talks with the Italian coach. Conte has now addressed the speculation, making clear that there are no advanced negotiations with any club at present.

Speaking as quoted by Calciomercato , Conte said:

"In light of the rumours published in recent days by various media outlets, both in Italy and abroad, I feel it's appropriate to intervene to clarify matters. My name has been linked to numerous clubs, but at the moment there are no advanced negotiations."After a splendid and successful stint at the helm of Napoli, I will take the time necessary to evaluate how and when to return to coaching. It will be a carefully considered decision, which I will make when I believe the conditions are right."

Conte's comments leave the door open to a future return to management but offer no indication that he is close to accepting either position. Juventus and Manchester United may continue to assess their managerial situations, while Conte intends to take his time before deciding on his next move.

articles.title: ESPN insider takes flamethrower to Miami’s ‘flammable’ defense that’s behind 0-3 start
articles.summary: The Miami Heat are off to a 0-3 start after their 115-110 loss to the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday evening, and an ESPN NBA insider has several specific con...
articles.body:
The Miami Heat are off to a 0-3 start after their 115-110 loss to the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday evening, and an ESPN NBA insider has several specific concerns about their defense. On the latest edition of the Hoop Collective podcast, hosted by Brian Windhorst, NBA insider Tim MacMahon took a "flamethrower" to Miami's "flammable" defense. In his rant, he cited defensive/net ratings to color his criticism.

"The Heat right now are an abysmal defensive team. They're the 3rd worst defensive team in the league. I'm going to read you defensive/net ratings for their starting lineup."

He then read off the defensive/net ratings:

Davion Mitchell: 130.4, -20.6 Klay Thompson: 134.9, -33.5 Andrew Wiggins: 141.5, -39 Giannis Antetokounmpo : 122.9, -28.6 Bam Adebayo: 128.3, -20.5

He continued, saying, "Their starting 5 is flammable right now. — They just aren't that talented out the top 2 guys. There's a pretty massive drop from 2-3 and then it's not a deep team. Klay Thompson's not a starter at this point in his life. Davion Mitchell's never been a starter on a good team. He should be playing 18 MPG or so."

In the Heat's loss against the Hornets, the team gave up 115 points and 16 three-pointers. Antetokounmpo also fouled out. Despite Giannis Antetokounmpo being unable to play in the rest of the game, the Heat almost pulled off a comeback, led by a lineup of Davion Mitchell and Bam Adebayo, with Bobby Portis Jr., Tim Hardaway, and Pelie Larsson. But the team was unable to pull off the comeback and head into Monday's matchup with the Dallas Mavericks winless on the season.

articles.title: JD Vance gives Bengals’ Ja’Marr Chase shoutout after Ravens blowout
articles.summary: Just days after JD Vance attended a Cincinnati Bengals practice, the team blew out their division rivals, the Baltimore Ravens, and the vice president is al...
articles.body:
Just days after JD Vance attended a Cincinnati Bengals practice, the team blew out their division rivals, the Baltimore Ravens, and the vice president is all in on the team.

The vice president celebrated the Bengals' latest win on social media , shouting out wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase , who scored a touchdown in the game, for taking note of his son's football gloves.

"Huge win for Cincinnati. Proud of the entire team, but special shout out to Ja'Marr Chase, an amazing talent, who made my little six-year-old's year by noticing his football gloves," Vance wrote. "It's early, but I think the Bengals are going to make a run. Who Dey!"

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Bengals erased a 13-0 deficit against the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens in Week 7, scoring 35 unanswered points. Joe Burrow passed for 292 yards and four touchdowns in the win. Chase caught five passes for 62 yards and a touchdown. Tee Higgins led the team with 148 yards and a touchdown.

Joe Burrow brushed off JD Vance's appearance at Bengals practice before beating Ravens

On Wednesday, Oct.21, Vance visited the Bengals at practice. Burrow barely acknowledged the vice president, saying they didn't have a chance to meet.

"He came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice," Burrow said about the vice president's visit.

"A lot of people around. That's what I love about what I do," said Burrow when asked about having everyone at practice. "It brings a lot of people together, and people want to take time out of their day to come and watch what we do, watch what I do, and watch all the work that I've put in to come and watch greatness. That's everybody in the locker room; that's why we do what we do. Whether it's on the TV, whether it's in-person, whether it's on the practice field, that's what we do."
